haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed in time, the every-minute sweep marks the hold EXPIRED and returns the stock to sale.
haiku-low.q2: Before the customer is charged. If one line is short, Inventory writes nothing, the order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and nothing is charged; cart kept.
haiku-low.q3: The idempotency key, which is the order id sent with the charge request. Repeating the request with the same key has no further effect.
haiku-low.q4: The order is cancelled as out of stock, the customer is emailed, and Payment is asked for a full refund keyed by order id.
haiku-low.q5: Only when the order is CONFIRMED, via the OrderConfirmed event. If checkout fails before that, the cart is kept and the customer can retry.
haiku-low.q6: The Order service runs checkout and moves it between steps. Its own database holds the order state, such as PAYMENT_PENDING or CONFIRMED.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined through its outbox to the broker for Order. The poll can also supply it.
haiku-low.q8: Payment's inbox table stores handled webhook event ids, so a repeat is skipped with 200. Whichever of webhook or poll arrives second finds the charge final and changes nothing.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined, Order calls ReleaseReservation over HTTP, and Inventory sets the hold RELEASED so stock goes back on sale.
haiku-low.q10: Order calls ClaimReservation. If the claim returns EXPIRED because the hold is not ACTIVE or is past expires_at, Order cancels and refunds; otherwise it confirms.
haiku-low.q11: The refund row stays FAILED in Payment, which retries with backoff and alerts on-call after N tries. The refund is never dropped silently. N is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: The Order service's OrderConfirmed event causes the Cart service to remove the ordered lines from the cart.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes. If not claimed, the sweeper (every minute) marks the ACTIVE hold EXPIRED and the stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging. If any line is short, Inventory writes nothing and returns the short items; Order sets REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK and shows them. Nothing reserved, nothing charged, cart kept.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) on the charge request: repeating it with the same key has no further effect. The retry rule itself is not set.
sonnet.q4: The claim returns EXPIRED; the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is emailed (cancelled, full refund), and Order asks Payment for a full refund (key = order id), which runs separately.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only after the order is CONFIRMED (on OrderConfirmed, ordered lines removed). If checkout fails, the cart is kept and the customer can try again.
sonnet.q6: The Order service runs checkout. The order's state (PLACED, PAYMENT_PENDING, etc.) is stored in the Order service's own DB.
sonnet.q7: Provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies the signature, updates the charge and publishes a PaymentSucceeded event via the outbox and broker to Order. A 5-minute poll of old PENDING charges is another path (its retention is an open question).
sonnet.q8: Payment's inbox of handled webhook event ids: a repeat event id gets a 200 and no change. A charge already final also changes nothing. Order also ignores PaymentSucceeded if state is not PAYMENT_PENDING or RESERVATION_EXPIRED.
sonnet.q9: Payment marks the charge DECLINED and publishes PaymentDeclined; Order sets PAYMENT_DECLINED and sends HTTP ReleaseReservation to Inventory, so the hold becomes RELEASED and stock goes back on sale.
sonnet.q10: Order sends ClaimReservation to Inventory. If the hold is ACTIVE and not past expires_at, it is CLAIMED and the order is confirmed; if it lapsed, Inventory returns EXPIRED and the order is cancelled and fully refunded.
sonnet.q11: The refund row stays FAILED, Payment retries with backoff and alerts on-call after N tries (N not stated). It is tracked in Payment's refund record, keyed by order id.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event published by Order; the Cart service removes the ordered lines (safe to repeat).
